messages.author: 3908a2da5354fc44
messages.subject: Answer to Bootstrap Error Question
parts:
FYI. Below are Jeff Laake's responses to my questions about bootstrap
errors. If you read the correspondence from the bottom to top it will
make more sense!

--
Duane R. Diefenbach, Ph.D.
Asst. Unit Leader - Wildlife
PA Coop. Fish & Wildlife Research Unit
113 Merkle Bldg.
University Park, PA 16802
http://pacfwru.cas.psu.edu/
(814) 865-4511 (phone)
(814) 863-4710 (fax)
dr...@psu.edu

Duane-

You can save the bootstrap statistics file, but you'll have to
manipulate it
yourself and unfortunately, it does not list which ones do not
converge. That
would be a useful addition. It is most likely the hazard function which
is not
converging. That key function is so flexible and it has some nasty
numerical
problems.

--jeff

"Duane R. Diefenbach" wrote:

> > Jeff,
> >
> > Thanks for the response. The analysis (w/o any bootstrapping)
indicated a
> > hazard (no adjustments) for 2 species and a half-normal (no
adjustments) for
> > another. I didn't fix the analysis to a single key fct for the
bootstrap, so I
> > assume it may be using a variety of them (I tested the half-normal,
uniform,
> > and hazard). The data are excellent in that they have a VERY broad
shoulder
> > (grassland songbirds). Maybe I'll try just using 1 key fct, but with
~4-5% not
> > converging the bootstrap CIs are very reasonable (it's only a problem
for 2 of
> > 4 analyses).
> >
> > If I have output from the bootstrapping saved to a file will it give
me stats
> > on specific runs?
> >
> >
> > Duane
> >
> > Jeff Laake wrote:
> >
>> > > Duane-
>> > >
>> > > All of the bootstrap values are used. In most cases if there is a
lack of
>> > > convergence, the parameters are still reasonable. Not certain if
one
>> > > approach is better thatn the other. I didn't like truncating out
cases
>> > > because of lack of convergence. I'd rather include that
uncertainty. What
>> > > key function are you using?
>> > >
>> > > --jeff
>> > >
>> > > "Duane R. Diefenbach" wrote:
>> > >
>>> > > > When using the bootstrap option with 500 bootstraps I received
about 25
>>> > > > warning messages of convergence failure. Does this completely
>>> > > > invalidate the use of CIs from the bootstrap procedure, or is the
number
>>> > > > of resampling runs reduced by the number of runs where convergence

>>> > > > failed? The help file is unclear on this point.
>>> > > >
>>> > > > I know from using the simulation procedure in SURVIV that it is
not
>>> > > > uncommon for a few runs to fail to converge because some
individual
>>> > > > resampled datasets are "weird"; however, these failed runs are
excluded
>>> > > > from the output. I noticed that DISTANCE still provide CIs when
you
>>> > > > have convergence problems, but the number of runs listed is the
same as
>>> > > > the input specification.
>>> > > >
>>> > > > Thanks,
>>> > > >
>>> > > > Duane
>>> > > >
>>> > > > --
>>> > > > Duane R. Diefenbach, Ph.D.
>>> > > > Asst. Unit Leader - Wildlife
>>> > > > PA Coop. Fish & Wildlife Research Unit
>>> > > > 113 Merkle Bldg.
>>> > > > University Park, PA 16802
>>> > > > http://pacfwru.cas.psu.edu/
>>> > > > (814) 865-4511 (phone)
>>> > > > (814) 863-4710 (fax)
>>> > > > dr...@psu.edu
> >
